title: OAuth authentication fails during token exchange with "Invalid code verifier"
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

OAuth authentication fails during token exchange with "Invalid code verifier" error in Streamlit 1.57.0, despite successful authorization. Downgrading to Streamlit 1.56.0 resolves the issue.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

# Define base pages (always visible)
pages = [
    st.Page("pages/home.py", title="Home", icon=":material/home:"),
]

# Add authenticated-only pages when logged in
if st.user.is_logged_in:
    pages.append(st.Page("pages/admin.py", title="Admin", icon=":material/admin_panel_settings:"))
    pages.append(st.Page("pages/usage_statistics.py", title="Usage Statistics", icon=":material/bar_chart:"))

# Sidebar widget
with st.sidebar:
    if st.user.is_logged_in:
        st.write(f"Welcome, **{st.user.name}**!")
        st.button("Log out", on_click=st.logout, use_container_width=True)
    else:
        st.button("Admin Login", on_click=st.login, use_container_width=True)

page = st.navigation(pages)
page.run()


Create pages/home.py with:

import streamlit as st

st.title("Home")
st.write("This is the home page.")
Create pages/admin.py with:

import streamlit as st

st.title("Admin")
st.write("This is the admin page.")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1.Configure Streamlit OAuth with an OIDC provider (i use [pocket id](https://github.com/pocket-id/pocket-id)) using secrets.toml with client_id, client_secret, server_metadata_url, redirect_uri, and client_kwargs = { "prompt" = "login" }.

2.Use st.login() and st.user.is_logged_in in the app.

3.Attempt login: authorization succeeds and redirects back with code, but token exchange fails.

### Expected Behavior

OAuth flow completes successfully, user is logged in

### Current Behavior

Authorization URL works, but token exchange raises:

authlib.integrations.base_client.errors.OAuthError: Invalid code verifier

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.57.0 (broken), 1.56.0 (works)
- Python version: 3.x
- OS: Windows
- Browser: Any
- Authlib version: 1.7.2


### Additional Information

_No response_

**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-15115)

### Analysis

This is a regression in Streamlit `1.57.0` where `st.login` fails during the OAuth token exchange with `authlib.integrations.base_client.errors.OAuthError: Invalid code verifier`. It reproduces against an OIDC provider that uses PKCE (here, [pocket-id](https://github.com/pocket-id/pocket-id)) and is resolved by downgrading to `1.56.0`.

**Likely root cause:** In `1.57.0`, Tornado was removed and Starlette became the default server (#14553). The new Starlette OAuth implementation in `lib/streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_auth_routes.py` introduced an in-memory `_AsyncAuthCache` (`_STARLETTE_AUTH_CACHE`) to hold Authlib's OAuth state between `/auth/login` and `/oauth2callback`. Authlib stores **both** the CSRF `state` value **and** the PKCE `code_verifier` in this same per-request entry, so whenever that cache entry is lost (worker restart, multi-process reload, the dev script-watcher reloading, etc.) the callback fails — sometimes as `MismatchingStateError`, sometimes (when PKCE is enabled, as it is for pocket-id) as `Invalid code verifier`.

This is the same underlying bug as #14991 ("OAuth MismatchingStateError regression in 1.57.0"), which was fixed by PR #15048 by removing the in-memory cache and switching to Authlib's session-based storage via Starlette's `SessionMiddleware`. The fix has landed on `develop` but is not yet released, so users on `1.57.0` are still affected. The fix should resolve this `Invalid code verifier` symptom as well; it would be good to confirm against `develop` or the next patch release.

### Related Issues

- [#14991 — OAuth MismatchingStateError regression in 1.57.0 (works in 1.56.0)](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/14991): Same root cause (lost OAuth state cache after Tornado removal in `1.57.0`), different symptom. Closed and fixed by [PR #15048](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15048) — this issue is very likely fixed by the same PR.
- [#12995 — st.login against MSAL returns authlib OAuthError AADSTS900144](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12995): Another `st.login` failure during the token exchange step in `authlib.fetch_access_token`. Different error message and provider, but the same code path and worth cross-referencing.
- [#11703 — Allow advanced customization of OIDC/OAuth2 parameters in `st.login()`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11703): Background on how `client_kwargs` (used in the repro) is plumbed into Authlib; relevant for understanding the OIDC config surface.

## Update: Root Cause Found!

After deeper investigation of PR #14553 (Tornado removal), I found the **actual root cause**:

### The Bug

When users configure PKCE via `code_challenge_method` in `client_kwargs`:
```toml
[auth.default]
client_kwargs = { code_challenge_method = "S256" }
```

The `code_challenge_method` is **never applied to the OAuth client**!

**Why:** Authlib's `OAUTH_CLIENT_PARAMS` doesn't include `code_challenge_method`, so it stays in `client_kwargs` dict but isn't extracted to set `client.code_challenge_method`.

**Result:** No `code_verifier` is generated or stored during login. But the OIDC provider (which auto-enables PKCE) expects one during token exchange → `Invalid code verifier` error.

### Why Tornado Worked

In Tornado (1.56.0), the same bug existed BUT:
- Tornado used a **server-side in-memory cache** for OAuth state
- The entire flow happened in-process without serialization
- The `code_challenge_method` might have been handled differently

### The Fix

I've added code to extract `code_challenge_method` from `client_kwargs` and set it directly on the client:

```python
# Extract code_challenge_method from client_kwargs if present
code_challenge_method = provider_client_kwargs.pop("code_challenge_method", None)

oauth = starlette_client.OAuth(config=_AuthlibConfig(config))
oauth.register(provider)
client = oauth.create_client(provider)

# Apply PKCE code_challenge_method if specified
if code_challenge_method:
    client.code_challenge_method = code_challenge_method
```

This ensures PKCE is properly enabled when configured.
